junction.name: Parkside Avenue & East Drive, New York City

claims.text: Parkside Avenue & East Drive had 82 injury crashes in police records since 2021-10-31: 37 pedestrians injured, 18 cyclists injured and 0 people killed.
At the U.S. DOT's values that harm costs about $5.6 million a year.
28% of crashes here had a pedestrian hurt, against 14% at the city's priority junctions.
Held up on later years: pedestrian hurt in 30% of crashes since 2024-05-01, against 15% at the city's priority junctions (found by the greedy search).

Held up on later years: a vehicle was going straight ahead, heading north and a two-wheeler was involved in 12% of crashes since 2024-05-01, against 4% at the city's priority junctions (found by the greedy search).

This corner got turn traffic calming in 2018. Across the city: a simple before/after says -26%, but a placebo date before the work shows a drop too, so the decline cannot be credited to the program. Repeating it here is not supported by the city's own record.

The city's Leading Pedestrian Interval signals: passed the causal gate (pedestrian injury crashes changed -17% (95% interval -22% to -11%) at 1,651 sites against sites treated later or the citywide trend, and a placebo date shows nothing).
The city's turn traffic calming: earlier trend (a simple before/after says -26%, but a placebo date before the work shows a drop too, so the decline cannot be credited to the program).
The city's enhanced crossings: not shown (at 96 sites the change in pedestrian injury crashes (-7%, 95% interval -50% to +69%) could be zero).
The city's speed humps: not shown (at 1,008 sites the change in injury crashes (+0%, 95% interval -9% to +9%) could be zero).

Backplates with Retroreflective Borders would avoid about 2.5 crashes a year (CMF 1410, the record FHWA's fact sheet cites; evidence: only if a site check confirms it), worth $842,000 a year; check on site: an entry on yellow or red.

Yellow Change Intervals would avoid about 1.3 crashes a year (CMF 4219, the more conservative of the two middle records of 4; evidence: only if a site check confirms it), worth $438,000 a year; check on site: an entry on yellow or red; the current yellow plus all-red time is below the ITE recommended practice.
The NYC Department of Transportation (NYC DOT) is responsible for Parkside Avenue, East Drive (not listed in NYSDOT Roadway Inventory, so a city street).
Who can push for it: Council Member, District 40, New York City Council; Brooklyn Community Board 14.
A request letter to the NYC Department of Transportation (NYC DOT) is drafted and checked.

draft_request.letter:
To: the NYC Department of Transportation (NYC DOT)
Cc: Council Member, District 40, New York City Council; Brooklyn Community Board 14
Subject: Request for safety study at Parkside Avenue & East Drive

Dear colleagues at NYC DOT,

We request a safety study at Parkside Avenue & East Drive on the roads you are responsible for — Parkside Avenue and East Drive — with timely fixes where warranted.

The official record for the 5 years from 31 October 2021 shows 134 crashes, including 82 injury crashes. Pedestrians injured: 37. Cyclists injured: 18. No one was killed. The harm is valued at $5.6 million per year in the U.S. DOT's official values for the cost of crashes (2024 dollars). The city lists this as a priority location. No safety work is recorded in the period; the last recorded work was turn traffic calming in 2020.

We ask you to assess high-visibility crosswalks on the approaches you own. High-visibility crosswalks are expected to prevent about 2.7 pedestrian injury crashes per year, avoiding about $937,000 in harm per year. It would pay for itself if kept to under $6.6 million per project, subject to the site check that the crossings are not already high-visibility. Please confirm the need and scope on site.

A Leading Pedestrian Interval is already recorded as in place.

Turn traffic calming was tried here in 2018. Across the city a simple before/after says -26%, but a placebo date before the work shows a drop too, so the decline cannot be credited to the program. The effect was not shown and repeating it here is not supported. Please consider a different approach.

Thank you for considering this request.

Sincerely,
[Your name]
[Your organisation or address]

Sources:
- NYC Open Data, Motor Vehicle Collisions - Crashes (h9gi-nx95)
- NYC DOT Street Improvement Projects (corridors); NYC DOT Street Improvement Projects (intersections); NYC Vision Zero View, Enhanced Crossings (6ax4-q5k4); NYC Vision Zero View, Leading Pedestrian Interval Signals; NYC Vision Zero View, Signal Timing/25 MPH Retiming; NYC Vision Zero View, Speed Humps (jknp-skuy); NYC Vision Zero View, Turn Traffic Calming; NYC Vision Zero priority corridors; NYC Vision Zero priority intersections
- FHWA CMF Clearinghouse, CMF 2697 (high-visibility crosswalks)
- U.S. DOT Benefit-Cost Analysis Guidance, 2026 Update, Table A-1 (2024 dollars)
